samples.summary: An unconfigured workspace ('' is the documented default) now makes every command fail with a misleading "Invalid identifier \"\"" error
samples.evidence: `seg()` rejects the empty string: `if (encoded === '' || DOT_SEGMENT.test(encoded)) throw ...`. `apiV1Base()`/`apiKeysUrl()` call `seg(config.workspace)`, and `resolveConfig()` (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:100, 126, 146, 164) falls back to `workspace: ''` in every one of its four branches when no `--workspace`, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`, session `activeWorkspace` or profile workspace is present. That is a normal pre-login state — config.ts:108 and test/config.test.ts:102 both explicitly describe the resulting `/api/v1/workspaces//documents` 404 as the behaviour of record. After this change, `wafflebase docs list` (and `--dry-run`, which also goes through `apiV1Base`) throws `Invalid identifier "": a URL path segment cannot be empty, "." or ".." — the URL parser resolves those...`, a message that names no identifier, does not mention the workspace, and offers no remedy (`wafflebase login` / `--workspace`). The failure is still a failure either way, but the diagnosis regressed for the most common misconfiguration.

samples.summary: The `%2e` alternatives in DOT_SEGMENT are unreachable, and the doc comment above it contradicts the code's own behaviour
samples.evidence: `DOT_SEGMENT = /^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i` is tested against `encoded = encodeURIComponent(value)`. `encodeURIComponent` always escapes `%` to `%25`, so the encoded string can never contain the literal substring `%2e`; only `.` and `..` can ever match. The `%2e`, `.%2e`, `%2e.`, `%2e%2e` arms are dead. Worse, the comment on lines 6–11 asserts "percent-encoding cannot smuggle a literal `..` through as data: `fetch` pops a path segment either way", which is false for the very case the new test asserts (test/http-client-paths.test.ts: input `%2e%2e` is sent as `%252e%252e` and preserved as data, not rejected). A comment that misstates the threat model on a guard is likely to mislead the next person who edits the regex.

samples.summary: Dry-run branches are placed outside the command's own try/catch in three commands but inside it in the rest, so `seg()`/`getConfig()` throws bypass the command-level error envelope
samples.evidence: `docs get` (docs.ts:126-129), `sheets cells get` (cells.ts:21-33) and `tabs list` (tabs.ts:15-18) put the `if (opts.dryRun)` block before `try {`, while `files get` (files.ts:114), `notes get` (notes.ts:83), `slides get` (slides.ts:88) and `api-keys *` (api-keys.ts:33/51/71) put it inside. In the first group a throw from `seg(docId)` or `resolveConfig()` escapes the action handler and is only caught by the last-resort `runCli` catch (cli.ts:77) — which the new test itself has to accommodate (`await expect(run(['docs','get','..','--dry-run'])).rejects.toThrow(...)` in read-dry-run.test.ts, versus the `api-keys revoke ..` case which is enveloped and exits 1). Any caller that drives the program via `parseAsync` rather than `runCli` (including the new test harness) gets a rejected promise instead of the documented `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope, and the two behaviours differ for otherwise identical commands.
